beats.text: Meet CodeGraph. It turns a multi-repo codebase into a live knowledge graph, and puts three workflows on top of it: view it, ask it, and fix it.
Everything is grounded in the graph, and a human approves every change to your code.

First, View Graph. Our product spans six repositories, about thirteen thousand symbols, and thirty-six thousand connections. Drawing all of that at once would be unreadable, so CodeGraph starts with the map.
Each box is a repository. Each arrow means one repo depends on another. Thicker arrows carry more links, and dashed arrows are inferred connections, like a front end calling an API in another repo.

Pick a repo, choose an entry point, and you get its neighborhood: what points at it on the left, and what it points to on the right. Here, one proxy route in discovery MFE fans out to eighteen endpoints in selection XAPI. No single repo shows you that.
beats.say: Pick a repo, choose an entry point, and you get its neighborhood: what points at it on the left, and what it points to on the right. Here, one proxy route in discovery M F E fans out to eighteen endpoints in selection X A P I. No single repo shows you that.

beats.text: The Tree view lets you browse any repo like a file explorer. Folders, files, classes and methods, one click at a time.
Next, Ask AI. Ask a question in plain English. Here: where is GlobalScriptsSDK used in tb-discovery-mfe?
beats.say: Next, Ask A I. Ask a question in plain English. Here: where is Global Scripts S D K used in discovery M F E?

beats.text: The agent is read-only. It can read, grep and glob files, and that is all. It starts from the graph to know where to look, then opens the real files to check.
In seconds you get an answer with real file names and line numbers. The SDK is mounted once, in the locale layout, at lines 217 to 227. The rest are tests and comments.
beats.say: In seconds you get an answer with real file names and line numbers. The S D K is mounted once, in the locale layout, at lines two seventeen to two twenty seven. The rest are tests and comments.

beats.text: The chips show which graph nodes the answer used, and a click jumps straight into the graph.
Finally, Fix Bugs. Paste the error. This one is a TypeError from the discovery front end: slugify cannot read toLowerCase of undefined. Then start the pipeline.
beats.say: Finally, Fix Bugs. Paste the error. This one is a Type Error from the discovery front end: slugify cannot read to lower case of undefined. Then start the pipeline.

beats.text: CodeGraph finds the function straight from the stack trace: slugify, in helpers formatters, in discovery MFE. It lists every file that imports it, and rules out same-named helpers in other repos.

beats.text: The agent then works through four gates, and nothing moves forward until a human approves. Gate one, analysis. Gate two, the root cause: a guard was removed in an earlier commit, and the scope fence stays on that one function.
Gate three is the proof: two tests fail on the unfixed code for the predicted reason, fifteen preservation tests still pass, and no source is changed before this gate.

Gate four is the smallest possible fix, one restored guard, and an open pull request. All seventeen tests pass. Approve it, and the run is done. The pipeline never merges: a person reviews and merges the pull request.
Every step leaves an artifact, so you review the reasoning, not just the diff. And any run can be paused, restarted or deleted.
See it. Ask it. Fix it. CodeGraph: the graph is the map, the code is the truth, and a human is always in the loop.
